statement: The legacy `.mjs` proof retention constant `DEFAULT_PROOF_RETENTION.pinPrReadyDays` (proof-storage.mjs) was declared but never read by `pruneProofRuns` -- a pinned run was permanently exempt from age-based pruning regardless of age. Faithfully porting `pruneProofRuns`'s literal logic to Rust (keep-set built from: pinned OR newest-N-per-proof OR newest-N-failed; remove-set built from age) reproduces this exact silent no-op unless the pin-age check is explicitly wired into `prunable_by_age`.
why: The workpack's G6 row explicitly calls out this divergence and requires a resolved (non-dead) behavior, not a faithful bug-for-bug port. A naive port would pass every legacy-shape test while still shipping a dead knob.
howToApply: `RetentionPolicy::prunable_by_age(pinned, age_days)` in crates/enforcer-proof/src/envelope.rs treats `pin_pr_ready_days` as a GRACE PERIOD for pinned runs (pinned runs become prunable past that age) rather than a permanent exemption. When porting any other legacy constant/config field during future arc work, check whether every declared field is actually READ by the corresponding legacy function before treating the port as behavior-preserving -- a field can be present in the JS source and simultaneously dead.

evidence.ref: src/proof-storage.mjs:10-16 (DEFAULT_PROOF_RETENTION declares pinPrReadyDays) vs src/proof-storage.mjs:357-399 (pruneProofRuns never reads pinPrReadyDays); resolved in crates/enforcer-proof/src/envelope.rs RetentionPolicy::prunable_by_age + crates/enforcer-proof/src/harness.rs prune_runs, proven by harness::tests::pinned_run_past_pin_pr_ready_days_becomes_prunable

statement: `prune_runs`'s per-proof-cap keep-newest rule (keep newest `max_runs_per_proof` runs for each proof id) ALWAYS wins over the age-based remove rule when a proof id has fewer total runs than the cap -- this is the legacy `pruneProofRuns` semantics (its `keep` set unconditionally wins over its `remove` set), not a bug. A test fixture with only 1-2 runs for a proof id can never observe age-based pruning in isolation: the per-proof cap rescues every run in a small set regardless of age.
why: My first age-based-pruning test fixtures used only 1-2 runs per proof id and failed, because the per-proof-cap keep-newest rule (`take(max_runs_per_proof)`) protected them even though they were past `prune_after_days`. This is not an implementation bug -- it faithfully matches proof-storage.mjs's `pruneProofRuns` (`keep` built from pinned + per-proof-cap + failed-cap; `remove` built from age; final = `remove && !keep`).
howToApply: To write a test that isolates the age-based prune path (or the pin-grace path) in this crate's `prune_runs`, PAD the target proof id with enough OTHER newer runs to push the run under test past the `max_runs_per_proof` cap (20 by default) -- otherwise the cap-based keep rule masks the age check entirely. See harness::tests::run_older_than_prune_after_days_is_removed_unless_pinned and pinned_run_past_pin_pr_ready_days_becomes_prunable in crates/enforcer-proof/src/harness.rs for the padding pattern.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-proof/src/harness.rs prune_runs + its test module; initial 2-run fixtures failed, fixed by padding to >20 runs per proof id before isolating the age-prune assertion

statement: The `ocentra-enforcer` MCP server reported itself stale (`ocentra_enforcer_coordination_claim` returned `directWritesAllowed:false, fallbackAvailable:true`) at session start, exactly as the orchestrator prompt anticipated. The documented fallback command (`ocentra_enforcer_run` invoking `scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination <subcommand>` from the FROZEN pack root, not this worktree) worked for `claim`, but its `mail` subcommand name in the orchestrator prompt does NOT exist -- the actual CLI subcommand is `message` (or `msg`), taking `--from/--to/--subject/--body`, confirmed by reading src/coordination/runner.mjs's `isCompatCommand`/dispatch table at the pack root.
why: Guessing subcommand names from a prompt's shorthand ("MAIL") against an unfamiliar CLI wastes a full round trip on a wrong invocation (`unknown command: mail`). The pack root's runner.mjs is authoritative over any prompt-level naming shorthand.
howToApply: When the coordination MCP tools are stale and the `ocentra_enforcer_run` fallback is needed, do not guess CLI subcommand names from an orchestrator prompt's colloquial phrasing (e.g. "MAIL") -- read `src/coordination/runner.mjs`'s dispatch table (`if (args[0] === ...)`) at the pack root (`C:\Projects\ocentra-enforcer`, distinct from the lane's worktree) first, or just try `message`/`msg` for send-a-note operations in this coordination CLI.

evidence.ref: C:\Projects\ocentra-enforcer\src\coordination\runner.mjs:71 (`if (args[0] === "message" || args[0] === "msg")`); no `mail` case exists anywhere in that dispatch table
